signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical De-risking
signals.text: AUD/JPY closed Friday at 104.90 as JPY dominated G10 performance (+1.852%, n=7) against broad AUD liquidation (-2.682%, n=4), establishing an extreme 4.534% bilateral spread. Reports that Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran combined with a VIX surge to 35.9 trigger sharp safe-haven flows into JPY, overwhelming the +362bp AONIA vs TONA carry cushion. Sydney and Tokyo opens will test downside momentum toward the 104.00 handle as retail remains 91% crowded long. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY into the open; extreme risk-off sentiment drives haven demand over carry yield. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market reopen following weekend Iran strike headlines. Risk: De-escalation headlines out of Washington or immediate bounce in equity futures back above Friday highs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — US Yield Slump vs Options Downside Hedging
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 158.56 as US 10-year Treasury yields plunged 14bp to 4.912% alongside a bull-flattening curve. Saxo 25-delta risk reversals reflect heavy downside demand at -1.77 put skew, running against leveraged funds short -29.5k JPY contracts. Falling US yields compress the +267bp SOFR vs TONA carry advantage, exposing the pair to rapid squeeze risk on the open. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY targeting 157.80. Catalyst: Tokyo open cash Treasury response to the 2.77% US 10Y intraday yield drop. Risk: US 10Y yield reclaims 5.00% or BoJ reinforces prolonged hold at the next BoJ meeting (mkt: 79% hike priced).

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded COT Short vs French Fiscal Distress
signals.text: EUR COT LF net short stands at -105.9k contracts (pctl 2, z -1.68), representing extreme institutional positioning as EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.0969. Fresh remarks from ECB officials warning of a French budget crisis add sovereign credit risk to European assets, while the +146bp SOFR over €STR carry advantage keeps dollar bids intact. S&P 500 selling (-3.70%) and widening Bund spreads keep upside capped despite BEER model valuation showing EUR/USD cheap at -2.80σ. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD with 1.0950 support vulnerable. Catalyst: European cash open assessment of French budget rhetoric ahead of the next ECB meeting (mkt: 85% hike priced). Risk: Short squeeze triggered by heavily crowded spec positions if eurozone fiscal fears abate.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Divergence Ahead of Retail Sales
signals.text: NZD Economic Surprise Index dropped to an extreme -25.5 while leveraged funds hold net short -23.9k contracts, confirming fundamental deterioration. Friday's close at 0.5469 sits below all key daily moving averages (SMA20 0.5579, SMA200 0.5800), with 93% retail long concentration presenting ongoing liquidation overhang. Upcoming Q3 New Zealand Retail Sales (forecast -0.2% q/q) provide the immediate test for continuation toward 0.5420. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD below 0.5500. Catalyst: New Zealand Q3 Retail Sales at 21:45 UTC Sunday. Risk: Retail Sales beat forecast (+0.5% q/q or higher) forcing short covering ahead of the next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 78% hike priced).
